title: PRESSER | Pete Golding - Mississippi State Preview (11-23-26)
text: I guess Pete, just from an injury standpoint, just where do you kind of see maybe Patrick and Cam and some other guys that you held out this past weekend? >> Yeah, I think uh you know, defensively we held out Cam. Uh feel like he'll be available this week. Uh today was more of a jog through tempo, but went through everything today. Uh still monitoring the hamstring, but I think he'll [snorts] be available. Um held out Will Echoes last week. Uh he went through practice today as well. I think he'll be available. Um I think Cudis will be game time decision. Um, I I think that's still got [clears throat] some work to do to be honest with you. Uh, I think Shakai will still be a game time decision. Um, I think it's it's better than we thought it was going to be at this point. Uh, he had a good weekend. Uh, talking to Pat yesterday, had a good day yesterday. Uh, so I think he's ahead of where we thought he was, but I think he'll it'll still be a game time decision. Now that you've gone through it, the Tom Luke speech and everything, just how important is it for this team with so many new faces to kind of instill the rivalry? >> Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, when you add 51 new guys, kind of like we were talking about on Saturday to a team, um, that aren't from this state, weren't recruited here out of high school and things like that, just for them to understand the history of it, um, you know, for us to have 18 guys in the room, you know, outside of our team that played here, uh, decided to come back here. So, I think hearing it from all of them, but uh there there's nobody that loves Old Miss more than Tom Luke and and when he gets up there, man, he gets fired up and gets into it. So, I I think they got a really good idea um yesterday evening of not only what it means to our former alumni uh but for the people of this state and also how it impacts the next 40 to 50 years, you know, and what this game means uh to all of our alumni and to all of our boosters. Um and, you know, I think Tai made a great point, you know, last night. He's like, "Yeah, I remember the wins and those are great, but he's like, "The one thing that haunts me is the one loss." And I think just making them understand, you know, how that always will follow you uh in this game. So, no, I thought he did an unbelievable job and I think our guys got a pretty clear understanding of how important it is. >> And to kind of follow up on that, you have a lot of Mississippi guys and in particular Perk and Will Eckles, them being Mississippi kids as well. Have you seen anyone in in the locker room give uh maybe something a little extra this week or speech or leadership wise? >> No, I mean I think you know that was a big part of last week. A lot of those guys of the cams of the wills you know even Jarius and all those guys like coach we want to make sure you know I know we got this week. I know we got to win the game but we want to make sure we're we're at 100% next week and we're full throttle because of what this game means to us and to this school and to this town. So, uh, I think, you know, a lot of them feel it from them and do realize growing up and and you got to pick a side and all those other things that go with it. So, I I think all of them, their attention to detail and all that's one thing, but holding the people accountable around them as well, uh, I think you'll see for sure. [snorts] Pete, last week when you made those changes and, uh, part of it you said was in regards to, you know, the retention stuff and getting work on that and getting ahead of next year's roster. Kind of where are the efforts with retain retention guys? You've already announced Bryson and do you anticipate some more announcements fairly soon? >> Yeah, I mean my big thing uh you know with all that is them understanding of hey how our feeling of them, how important they are to us moving forward and all those things. Uh and it's really just to start the negotiation process uh knowing normally the guy that you're meeting with and talking about it um is not going to really control it at the end as far as when it actually finishes. Um, so, uh, I think the agent negotiation component of it and all that, I think the earlier that you start that, I think the better. Um, but we we haven't put a target date on any of those guys and trying to get it done by by this Friday or by next week or anything like that. It was just I understood what last year looked like and the later you wait, um, you know, the bowl game starts coming up and other things start kind of sneaking up on you. Um, so, um, I think naturally there's a lot of them that are really good places. uh they've, you know, communicated this is where they want to be here, you know, or be here for a lot of them. So, uh I think a lot of them will get done sooner than later hopefully. >> You said after the uh game Saturday that you kind of enjoyed the arrangement with B Brown calling the plays and you doing other things. Uh are you going to do that this week as well? >> No, this week I'm I'm going to call this one. Um uh I think you know last week allowed me you know part of allowing uh coach Brown last week to call it was the retention component but also working ahead on Mississippi State. Um and so that allowed me you know to kind of get ahead on a lot of the tape and and some from the game planning things and all those type of things. So um just the experience within this game and versus this offense and coach Levby and all that type of stuff. Um that that was for last week. You're not a lawyer, so I hope this is a fair question, but do you know if you have to like do you have to change the the retention contracts or or any of that just with what happened with with Prince Will and Devin Harper last year? >> Well, so so the SEC has done that, you know, so that was the big thing in the offseason uh you know to make it look like some of those other conferences um you know that once those guys sign from a retention standpoint to come back that um you know they forego the portal window u from that standpoint. Uh so uh the SEC in the offseason, you know, Sanki and all them did a lot of work, you know, in the spring and the summer to reset how all those contracts are. So it's not based on the independent school now. It comes straight from the SEC office. We're all under the same umbrella. Um so um that's kind of what you're reading about some of those agents that are real fired up about it. So but that uh that that's not our doing that. That's the conference is doing. But it's definitely got, you know, a lot of the language in there um to once you decide this, it protects both sides within reason. [snorts] >> Coach, what are you anticipating facing Mississippi State on Friday? >> Yeah, anticipating their best. You know, I mean, I think, uh, you know, this is one of those games. Um, you know, obviously it's a playin game for them as well. And, uh, what it means, um, not only from a head coaching standpoint, from the players and everything else that they're going to try to find every way humanly possible to win the football game. And I think the biggest thing to our players, you know, is always what you see on tape prior to this game is not what you're going to see on Friday. You know, there's gonna be a different energy. Um, you know, they're going to scheme everything they possibly can. They're going to try to steal every possession they possibly can. So, um, forget what you see, you know, on tape and Tai mentioned that last night that they're going to come in here ready to roll. Uh, this game means a lot to them as well and so we're going to have to be at our best. So, really good preparation this week and have good plans in all three phases. uh and go in there and you know go out there and execute at a high level because it's going to take it. >> Question. >> Yeah. Coach, when you have multiple guys on Mississippi State who can run 101, 10200s, 21 second 200s, you know, how do you approach that from a def defensive perspective? Do you play more kind of man coverage? Do you, you know, feel confident in your defense defensive backs to do that or do you focus more on zone coverage for that matchup? Well, first off, I'm just glad we're not running track. But, um, no, I think a lot of things, obviously, they're very explosive, and I think when you look at their games that they have success, you know, creating explosive plays, uh, has been a big part of their success, you know, on offense. So, you've got to be really smart where a couple of these guys are. Um, you know, regardless whether you're playing man or zone of understanding what are you're inviting. Um, I think affecting their quarterback is important. Uh, obviously they lost their starter. So, they've been kind of rolling through a couple of those guys. Um, but I don't think you could come out of the game saying, "Hey, you look up and three beat you." You know, I think Seven's got elite speed like you're talking about. You know, a lot of guys on the perimeter can really run. So, I think you got to do a good job, you know, changing up the coverage and giving them some help and rolling guys over the top, but there's going to be times that you're going to have to play manto man to stop the run. Uh, that you got to be smart with who's on them and what's their depth and where's their help and all those type of things. So, uh, I think it's been, you know, pretty consistent over the last couple years with Lebby. You know, if it's not going right, they're going to get in 12, shrink the formation, put the speed outside and isolate it and and make you decide what are you going to do. You going to try to stop the run and load the box and leave the guy one-on-one or not. So, we'll have some times that that'll probably happen that we're going to have to, you know, be smart and be technically sound and be able to make the play, but we also got to be able to give him some help. >> Pete, you got two more games with Trinidad, but then, uh, you you got to find another quarterback. What has Duce shown, you know, for for his time here for the year and then last, you know, last game just what you saw out of him and getting some pass opportunities and how's he doing health-wise? >> Yeah. Uh, I think number one, what I've seen from Duke since he's been here, he's been a sponge. You know, I think Joe's done a really good job with him. Uh, he knows that he had a developed play in the position. Uh, that it's not always about being the biggest and the fastest. It's not always about pulling the ball down. So, I've been really, uh, impressed with his progression within the offense and understanding, um, protections and concepts and coverages and all those things. So, I think he's really developed as the quarterback. Um, I've always said that that there there's a moxy about Deuce that's a little different. Uh, he's got a quiet confidence about himself and I think that's shown up when he's gone in and I think he's got competitive character. Um, and when he comes in, you know, he's really, really productive. So, uh, I was glad to see him, you know, check a couple things within the game. Um, I thought he made a couple of elite throws and stood in there and put the ball on time. Um, and then obviously he's different when he does break the pocket a little bit. So, uh, I hate that the hamstring, you know, got tweaked when it did, you know, wanted to see more. Obviously, you know, was hopeful that he was going to get some multiple quarters, but was also excited for Walker and what he's meant to this program and our team from a leadership standpoint for him to go in. But I think Duce is continuing to develop as a quarterback. Um, obviously, you know, in this league, you're going to need multiple guys in that room. You know, you're a snap away from the next guy being up, which a lot of these teams showed. So, uh, he's going to continue have to develop and, um, I think we got an elite high school guy right now that we got to make sure we hang on to as well. Um, but, uh, really proud of where he is. >> Last year there was a lot going on around the Egg Bowl. Um, obviously you were in a different position. and everyone was trying to figure out what Lane was going to do. I'm just curious, how different is life for you this year? >> Yeah. Um I don't know. It depends what day you asked me. Uh but obviously I wasn't doing this last year this time. Um no. Um, you know, I kind of thought about that a little bit, you know, the other day of what this weekend was last year and the ride back and all that and just, you know, the indecision, kind of the unknown, but um, you know, now it's kind of kind of settled in and got a good idea of, you know, what it needs to look like moving forward, you know, and I think, you know, we kind of talked about this a couple weeks. I mean, it's it's my responsibility. It's our responsibility to make sure we're doing everything for the program, uh, to give us our best shot. And [clears throat] so, uh, making a lot of decisions, you know, that you weren't in charge of last year, uh, what that needs to look like moving forward, but also an appreciation, um, as well for having the opportunity to, to do what I do on a daily basis, and, um, really grateful [clears throat] for the guys that we do have in the locker room. I told you from the very beginning, really good group of dudes. Um, we haven't always got them to execute the way that we need to on a consistent basis, but, I've really, really enjoyed being around them. Uh, I've really enjoyed being able to impact other people's lives as far as from an assisted coaching standpoint and seeing what this year's meant to them. I think this week reminds me of that of all those Old Miss guys that came back and how grateful they are for this opportunity this week to go play in another egg bowl and coach in an Egg Bowl. So, uh, really, really grateful, but understanding that, uh, there's a lot of responsibility that comes with it, too, and make sure that we're doing everything that we can moving forward to put ourselves in the best spot. Pete, based on your recruiting right now, are you trying to get less uh dependent on the portal than than you've been been in the last three or four years? >> You know, I mean, I've said this for a while and I've tried to do this defensively since we've been here. You know, when when you've got stability and systems, I you want to work it from the ground up and you want to get elite high school players and get them in here to understand your system, but also to understand your culture, right? So when you do bring other guys in that have to play winning football right now, uh they mold to them, you know, and and they're not looking around. It's like, who's going to tell me what to do, how do I do it, and all those type of things. So that's always been a big piece of us defensively. I think you can see that by the guys that run out there. Um but that that's a team model for us. Now, they've got to be good enough to play winning football in the SEC, you know, so you got to recruit at an elite level uh to do that. So, we're we're not going to just go to the high school rank just to get a high school player if we don't think he can play winning football in the SEC. It's not my goal for him to do that his freshman year. I don't think that's realistic. You know, I've had a couple freshman in the past that that have started as true freshman. They're top 10 draft picks. It's hard to come in here in 18 and play productive winning football in this league um based on the position that you play. So, uh I think there's a balance like in everything. I think a lot of the balance is dependent upon your retention. Uh which is the struggle now because you're signing guys in December and not really knowing the retention model until January. Um you know, so that piece you got to really really make sure that high school class uh is wired the right way and they're good enough to play winning football in the SEC. And I think this group is, but but absolutely I want to build it from the ground up from a high school standpoint with elite players uh that want to be here uh that want to play in these systems and want to get developed um and want to be at Old Miss. Um and then once you look at the January model, how many starters do you have coming back? Um and then what starters, you know, do you not have coming back that you need to go to the portal and replace cuz they got to make an impact immediately. Um and I think that model is not strictly based on tape. I think that model, the competitive character and who they are, um, and the love of the game, I think matters more now than ever. And I think we got to do a really, really, really good job from a portal standpoint of not evaluating the tape, more importantly, evaluating the competitive character, uh, and how much they love football. >> I know it wasn't against a powerful opponent, but what did you think how Perkins looked after looking on the film and what kind of made the last two weeks the right time to make that permanent change for him? Yeah, you know, obviously, you know, him coming out of high school, his first camp here, he played stag backer, you know, so that first August, uh, we put him at the money backer in this defense. Um, and knew at that age, um, coming from Raleigh and all that, like it it was going to be a lot, you know, athletically, from a skill set standpoint and all that, it was he can do it, you know, really naturally instinctive, really good trigger. He's got unbelievable balance and body control, you know, from a contact standpoint. Uh but just the the mental piece of it's not all C ball get ball, right? We got a run responsibility and a coverage responsibility and some of those things. It was a lot for him. But at that point in 23, he was too good of a player to keep off the field. And so that's why we moved him to the jack position. A lot less thinking, right? We're either going to rush you or drop you in here. You're a buzz player, you're a hook player, and that's it. Um and when he was down there, he was he's so much more heavierhanded than you think regardless of his body type and his size. Um and then you know when you look up he's got really good at the position we have the ability to move him around and use him as a spy and all those type of things. It was still hard at that point to get elite edge guys multiple you know I think the plan kind of last year was hey if we can go get the right edge guys uh that was a big piece of the Pete Wel getting him to come back. This was the talk of going into last offseason, you know, to move him cuz what I promised him his freshman year once he moved the Jag is like, "Look, man, that last year I'm moving you whether you want to be moved or not because I know what your future's going to look like and it's not going to be at the position you're playing." And so, uh, that's my responsibility to you and he knows that. He understands that, you know, for what his future looks like. So, um, you know, that was the goal for kind of last offseason. It didn't work out that way. Um, but that would be definitely the goal moving forward. So, the timing of it, uh, was because of Katon, [snorts and clears throat] right? So, once Katon went down, um, and we had a three-man rotation at backer, which you have to have, you know, in this league right now. Once he went down, you know, I felt like he was our best option to play winning football at the position on top of this would give him a couple weeks, you know, to really see, hey, is this something I want to do? Is this something that I can do? and start giving him the confidence moving forward that this is the right decision for his future. And so that was the timing of it. Um but no, loved it, man. Uh you know, we we try to be a little simpler when he was in, but uh he's a piece that you can still blitz. We know we know he can do that. Uh he's got a leak coverage ability, you know, it's just the understanding of the concepts and some of those things. Uh he's been much more natural in the box than you would think that transition, you know, this late in the season, but did some good things in the run game as well. So, uh, he'll be full time there moving forward. >> Any questions for coach? >> Talk us about talk to us about where you think Jacobe Hubson is um in his development. >> Yeah. Um, I I thought in camp I thought uh Jacobe had a had a good camp. I thought he improved. Um, you know, one thing in the offseason that I really talked to him about was his hip flexibility and short area quickness. you know, that was something that, you know, playing DB and quarterback, you know, out of high school, that money position for us is a very athletic position. You know, that position plays in space a lot. Uh, and I think that's one thing in this league, you know, you got to be able to get the the ball carrier on the ground in space. And that's been the one thing when he started putting on some weight in the spring, kind of looked up and now he's 245 and he ain't running the same. And so, I thought he did a good job in the summer and in fall camp, you know, of getting that body right. Paul did a good job with him getting him back down. Um I thought he had a good camp and then you know given some opportunities earlier in the year was disappointed in his finishing ability, was disappointed in the physicality at the point of attack and some block protection. Uh so we called him in like look man this is our focus needs to be on we need to do a good job setting those drills up and all those type of things. So uh he he's consistently working through that. So I think I think it's flashed a little bit but I think the hip flexibility still shows up a little bit. I think the offseason, you know, is going to be really big for him. Uh, and the physicality at the point of attack is something that's got to continue to improve. >> Last one up top. >> Yeah, coach, you talked a lot at the beginning of the season. I think it might have been your first press conference about your relationship with coach Levby. I guess what what has the communication been like with him prior to this week and you know, I guess what is it like going up against a guy like that that you know, means so much to you? >> Yeah, I mean I think the last time that I I talked to him, I didn't talk to him. I just text him was when when he reset the quarterback market. So I told him appreciate that. Um but uh hadn't really talked to him since then. Uh but no, lot of respect for Lebby. Um good friend of mine. He's an elite coach. I mean, I think when you watch him on tape right now, you can look at the scores and you look at the stats, but what what he's get he's getting him in the right plays. He's got the right call and they're checking the right things, right? There's dude, they got it right. Sometimes the ball doesn't get delivered there and he gets sacked or what have you. But uh I think he I think he's an elite OC. I think he has been for a long time. Uh, I like him as a dude. I think he's a really good dude. I think he treats his staff the right way. Um, you know, I think he's got the right mentality. Uh, so I know it hasn't gone exactly how he's seen it go and and they've had some injury issues. Obviously, you lose your quarterback, it's really tough in this league. Um, regardless, but always had a lot of respect for him more more because of the person that he is, uh, to be honest with you. And we're both super competitive, you know, so last time I saw him, we were both on a golf course, you know, together. But, uh, you know, this week be the grass. So, I know he's going to try to whoop my ass this week. I'm going to try to whip his. So, uh, wish him all the luck in the world, just not this week. >> All right. Thanks, guys.
